story.c1.s1.title: Sign the ledger
story.c1.s1.body: Marla Thistlebrew slides a ledger across the bar, already open to a fresh page. "Name, class, next of kin. The last one's optional, but the bookbinder charges by the line either way."
story.c1.s1.done: Your name is in the book. The book, Marla notes, has never lost anybody. Recently.
story.c1.s2.title: Run three errands
story.c1.s2.body: The three notices nobody has taken are a fence, a rumor, and something in a sack. Marla says everyone starts with the sack; nobody has ever explained why.
story.c1.s2.done: Three notices, three ticks in the ledger. The sack is not discussed again.
story.c1.s3.title: Wear what you found
story.c1.s3.body: You have been carrying a perfectly good piece of equipment in a bag for an hour. Marla has watched this happen the entire time and has decided to say something.
story.c1.s3.done: Equipment: on you now, rather than near you. Marla goes back to polishing, satisfied.
story.c1.s4.title: Spend an attribute point
story.c1.s4.body: "Training is deciding what you'd like to be better at and then paying for it," Marla says. "Same as everything." She points you at the ledger's back pages, where the sums live.
story.c1.s4.done: One point spent, and something about standing up is measurably easier than it was this morning.
story.c1.s5.title: Face Krellbor
story.c1.s5.body: Krellbor the Overconfident has beaten every newcomer in Brambleford this season, chiefly by fighting only newcomers. The crowd would like this streak to end. So would the crowd's bookmaker.
story.c1.s5.done: Krellbor takes it well, loudly, at length, to anyone who will hold still. You have a title now.
story.c2.s1.title: Ask about the noises
story.c2.s1.body: Something beneath The Gilded Tankard has been rearranging the barrels by size. Marla would call it charming if it hadn't started on the good vintages.
story.c2.s1.done: Marla concedes there is a cellar. She had been hoping to get through the season without using the word.
story.c2.s2.title: Find the cellar key
story.c2.s2.body: The key went missing four innkeepers ago and has been sighted since in a stew, a magpie's nest, and a debt. Take enough work around town and it surfaces.
story.c2.s2.done: The key is yours. It smells faintly of stew. Nobody in Brambleford wants to talk about the magpie.
story.c2.s3.title: Clear the first floor
story.c2.s3.body: The top floor of the Rat Cellars is less a cellar than a lobby. There is a rota pinned to the wall, and your name is not on it.
story.c2.s3.done: Floor one cleared, rota confiscated. The handwriting was distressingly neat.
story.c2.s4.title: Meet Hammond Forgebright
story.c2.s4.body: "Rats," says Hammond Forgebright, not looking up. "You'll want reach, then. And a shorter temper than the one you came in with." He is a weapon smith; this is his version of a warm welcome.
story.c2.s4.done: Hammond sells you something with reach. He declines to offer a warranty, and mentions this twice.
story.c2.s5.title: Reach the third floor
story.c2.s5.body: Deeper down, the barrels stop being barrels and start being furniture. Whatever runs this operation has opinions about soft furnishings.
story.c2.s5.done: Three floors down, the cellar is quiet. Marla has already re-shelved the good vintages, purely as a precaution.
story.c3.s1.title: Hear the wardrobe rumor
story.c3.s1.body: A traveling tailor drinking at the Tankard swears that matched armor makes a person measurably harder to hit. Petra Stoutstitch, two stools down, does not disagree, which is the alarming part.
story.c3.s1.done: You have written down the word "set." Petra has written down your measurements.
story.c3.s2.title: Reach the fifth floor
story.c3.s2.body: Floor five is where the rats keep everything they have taken off adventurers, sorted by size and, unsettlingly, by taste.
story.c3.s2.done: The hoard is yours. A surprising amount of it matches.
story.c3.s3.title: Claim a matched piece
story.c3.s3.body: Somewhere down there is a piece made by a smith who cared. You will know it because it will make everything else you own look like it was finished on a deadline.
story.c3.s3.done: One matched piece, one small ceremony, one extremely smug tailor across town.
story.c3.s4.title: Take the forge lesson
story.c3.s4.body: Old Coalbeard hands you a hammer, then takes it straight back. "Not yet. First you watch. Then you pay. Then, if the mood holds, you hammer."
story.c3.s4.done: Your gear is one notch better and your purse is one notch lighter. Coalbeard calls this balance.
story.c3.s5.title: Wear two matched pieces
story.c3.s5.body: Two pieces of a set worn together do something the tailors refuse to explain and the Arcanum refuses to fund research into. It works regardless, which annoys everybody.
story.c3.s5.done: For the first time, you look like you meant to dress this morning.
story.c4.s1.title: Ask about the crypt key
story.c4.s1.body: Marla's family kept a crypt out past the salt flats. "Kept" is doing a great deal of work in that sentence; the sea has since taken an interest in the property.
story.c4.s1.done: The crypt key is cold and wet, and was cold and wet before you touched it.
story.c4.s2.title: Enter the Sunken Crypt
story.c4.s2.body: The Sunken Crypt has been underwater for four centuries and its residents have made their peace with that. They would like you to make peace with it too, permanently.
story.c4.s2.done: First floor cleared. Your boots will never be the same, and arguably neither will you.
story.c4.s3.title: Sail to Castaway Cove
story.c4.s3.body: Marla points at a boat. "The crypt is a family matter. The Cove is where the family's things washed up. Go and be embarrassing about it on my behalf."
story.c4.s3.done: You come back salt-crusted, sunburnt, and holding something that was very clearly somebody's.
story.c4.s4.title: Reach the third hall
story.c4.s4.body: Three floors down the water stops rising and starts waiting. The dead here do not attack so much as make room, as though you were expected and are running late.
story.c4.s4.done: Third floor cleared. Far below, something pale is keeping time, and it is in no hurry whatsoever.
story.c4.s5.title: Recover the Regalia
story.c4.s5.body: The Thistlebrews were somebody once, and had the outfit to prove it. Marla insists she does not care. Marla has also described the shoulder pieces from memory, twice.
story.c4.s5.done: Marla holds the regalia a long moment, then hands it back. "Suits you. Don't get it wet." It is already wet.
story.c5.s1.title: Hear Fenn out
story.c5.s1.body: Fenn Whistlewick's Menagerie currently contains one deeply disappointed owl and a great deal of empty straw. "I don't need much," he says. "Three friends. Any three, honestly."
story.c5.s1.done: You have agreed to catch animals for a man who names each pen before anything lives in it.
story.c5.s2.title: Befriend a Moss Boar
story.c5.s2.body: The Moss Boar is not fast, not clever, and not remotely worried about you. Fenn says the trick is to sit down nearby and be boring for a while.
story.c5.s2.done: The Moss Boar follows you home. It has decided you are a slow-moving shrub, and it is very fond of shrubs.
story.c5.s3.title: Recruit a Pebble Golem
story.c5.s3.body: Pebble Golems happen when a rockslide has a good idea. Fenn maintains the good idea is friendship. Zinnia Vex maintains it is a filing error nobody has been brave enough to correct.
story.c5.s3.done: It fits in a satchel. It would rather not. It is coming along anyway.
story.c5.s4.title: Coax down a Dream Moth
story.c5.s4.body: Dream Moths are drawn to people with something on their mind. Fenn considers this a compliment. Marla, who has met a number of adventurers, considers it a diagnosis.
story.c5.s4.done: The moth settles on your pack and dreams, loudly, about lamps.
story.c5.s5.title: Choose a companion
story.c5.s5.body: Three pens full, one road ahead, and Fenn will not let you take all of them. "Pick one. The others get treats and a nap. It is a good life, honestly. I'd take it."
story.c5.s5.done: Somebody is walking beside you now. Fenn waves until you are out of sight, then keeps waving.
story.c6.s1.title: Fetch the Hollows key
story.c6.s1.body: The Ironroot Hollows were sealed by people who carved DO NOT on the door and then, in much smaller letters, an apology. The key hangs in the Tankard, above the good vintages.
story.c6.s1.done: The key is heavier than a key needs to be. So, on reflection, is the apology.
story.c6.s2.title: Break into the Hollows
story.c6.s2.body: Ironroot's first floor is a root system that has learned to hold a grudge. It has been holding this particular one since before Brambleford had a name.
story.c6.s2.done: One floor in. The roots draw back — not beaten, exactly. Considering.
story.c6.s3.title: Push out to Sunscorch
story.c6.s3.body: The Hollows drink from somewhere, and every map agrees that somewhere sits under Sunscorch: country so dry the mile-markers have given up and started lying about the distance.
story.c6.s3.done: Sunscorch is open to you. Bring water. Bring considerably more water than that.
story.c6.s4.title: Learn your elixirs
story.c6.s4.body: Zinnia Vex pours three things into a fourth thing and hands it over without eye contact. "Drink it. Feel briefly excellent. Come back when the excellent wears off."
story.c6.s4.done: You feel briefly excellent. Zinnia writes down exactly how briefly, for reasons she declines to share.
story.c6.s5.title: Reach the heartwood
story.c6.s5.body: Five floors down there is a chamber where the roots grow in rows, pruned and tended. Something has been gardening down here. Something with staff.
story.c6.s5.done: The heartwood splits. Pinned inside is a pale seal — a court's crest, pressed into living wood by somebody who never came back up.
story.c7.s1.title: Obtain the Spire key
story.c7.s1.body: The Obsidian Spire has no door at ground level, which the architects called a security feature and the surveyors called a lawsuit. The key opens the ninth floor. You will be starting at the first.
story.c7.s1.done: You now hold a key to a door you cannot reach. In Brambleford this is considered an ordinary Tuesday.
story.c7.s2.title: Enter the Obsidian Spire
story.c7.s2.body: The Spire is glass the whole way up, and the glass remembers. Each floor shows you the last person who tried this, right up to the part where they stopped.
story.c7.s2.done: Floor one. Your reflection climbed alongside you and looked, frankly, more confident about the whole business.
story.c7.s3.title: Climb into the top hundred
story.c7.s3.body: The Spire's wardens only respect a name they have heard shouted. Marla suggests the arena. "Get famous enough to be annoying. It is a skill, and you have the face for it."
story.c7.s3.done: Top one hundred in Aethermoor. Somewhere below, Krellbor is telling people he taught you everything.
story.c7.s4.title: Reforge something properly
story.c7.s4.body: "Anyone can improve a thing once," says Old Coalbeard. "Improving the same thing five times is where you learn whether you are stubborn or merely rich."
story.c7.s4.done: One item, five times better, and Coalbeard almost nods. Almost.
story.c7.s5.title: Reach the fifth floor
story.c7.s5.body: Halfway up, the glass stops reflecting you and starts reflecting somewhere else: a long hall, a thin throne, and a court standing very still, waiting on a guest.
story.c7.s5.done: Five floors of Spire behind you. Your reflection did not climb with you this time. It went on ahead.
story.c8.s1.title: Accept the invitation
story.c8.s1.body: The invitation arrives at the Tankard in an envelope nobody saw delivered, addressed to you in your own handwriting. Marla reads it twice and pours you something strong and free.
story.c8.s1.done: The key was inside the envelope. So was a seating plan. You are seated last.
story.c8.s2.title: Enter the Pale Court
story.c8.s2.body: The Pale Court keeps its lamps lit for guests who never arrive and its cutlery polished for meals it never serves. The gatekeeper takes your coat. You were not wearing a coat.
story.c8.s2.done: You are inside. Somewhere ahead of you, a very long table is being laid for two.
story.c8.s3.title: Reach Duskgate
story.c8.s3.body: The court's writ runs to the edge of the map, and the edge of the map is Duskgate — the last town in Aethermoor, where the roads end politely and the light stops trying.
story.c8.s3.done: Duskgate opens. Its innkeeper has heard of Marla and asks, carefully, whether she is still angry.
story.c8.s4.title: Cross the fifth hall
story.c8.s4.body: Halfway through the court the guests stop pretending to be furniture. They are not hostile. They are relieved. Somebody has finally come to take the seat at the end.
story.c8.s4.done: Five halls done. The music has stopped, and every face in the court has turned toward the same door.
story.c8.s5.title: Take your seat
story.c8.s5.body: The Pale King has waited a very long time to be interrupted. He is unfailingly polite about it, which is somehow worse, and he pulls out your chair himself.
story.c8.s5.done: The ballad of Brambleford ends on a chair pushed back, a court exhaling, and Marla — a very long way north — pouring one out for a name she once wrote in a ledger.
